sourceOccurrences.label: Pointwise critical two-point estimate
sourceOccurrences.note: The source states the pointwise form for radial kernels; constrained and unrestricted connections are distinguished.

proofUses.reason: The upper envelope gives a finite row sum, so FF30 supplies a finite positive critical intensity with bounds depending only on d, L, alpha, c, C, subcritical finiteness and boundary flux; 12NL supplies rooted damping. Then 655W and 7YNX give pointwise shell bounds at the critical intensity with uniform constants, and summing over shells gives the averaged bounds.

A radial kernel is symmetric and, by the upper envelope, integrable, so the argument for J98J applies: FF30 gives 1/B <= beta_c < infinity, where B is the finite row sum, together with the quantile bound and boundary flux; L0TE gives subcritical finiteness; 12NL gives rooted damping; 655W bounds the block means; and 7YNX gives pointwise bounds at every vertex of each shell, with constants depending only on d, L, alpha, c, C. Translation invariance moves a general pair x, y to 0, y - x and the ball Lambda(x, y) to Lambda_n; the case x = y is trivial.
For n at least 1, multiplying the averaged chain of J98J by the ball volume gives both bounds on the full-cluster mass in the ball for every symmetric kernel; for n = 0 the sum is 1.
The first inequality of J98J times the ball volume gives the lower bound for the restricted cluster; the upper bound holds because the restricted cluster is contained in the full cluster.
